reason: The cited evidence (E1) describes Mg-Ti-Zn alloys with intermetallic phases and good corrosion resistance linked to a TiO2-rich film, but it does not address a metastable solid-solution initial state, diffusion-driven precipitation upon aging, or the effect of precipitate size/distribution on oxide integrity. The key premises thus lack specific prior support.
premises: Mg-containing lightweight HEA can be produced in a metastable homogeneous solid-solution state
Thermal aging triggers diffusion-driven nucleation and growth of Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates
Fine, dispersed Mg-rich intermetallics reinforce the protective oxide film and retain corrosion/oxidation resistance
Coarsened intermetallic networks disrupt oxide scale continuity and degrade environmental resistance
A critical thermal threshold separates moderate (benign) from aggressive (degrading) aging regimes
